transcript.summary: Fixed an operator-precedence bug in `src/parser.mjs`: the constant arrays defining the additive/multiplicative operator sets were swapped. `parseAddSub` was looping over `['*', '/', '%']` and `parseTerm` over `['+', '-', '||']`, so `parseAddSub` (the higher-precedence tier called from `parseComparison`) consumed the multiplicative operators while `parseTerm` consumed additive ones — fully inverting precedence (e.g. `2 + 3 * 4` evaluated to 20 instead of 14). I swapped the two arrays so `parseAddSub` uses `['+', '-', '||']` and `parseTerm` uses `['*', '/', '%']`. All 6 tests now pass (`npm test` exits 0).
